conviction_note: abs_move 12.0 (straddle 12.64%, own median 10.31%, new Q4 guide and a CFO who started three days before the print) times a near-coin-flip p_up of 51. Two small things lean up: the stock was de-risked about 11% in five sessions into the print with calls bid and short interest rising, and Q4 comps ease. Against that, this name has sold four of its last five prints on the guide despite revenue beats, and the Europe cross-border drag continues. The findings sum to +1.5 while the scaled number is +0.24: the findings are each small and sourced, and the reaction history makes the sign close to a coin flip.
bar: Q3 revenue: company guide $1,190-1,210m (+13-15%) and adj. EBITDA $335-355m (Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001506293/000150629326000102/q2-26xpressrelease.htm). Revenue consensus $1.21bn, from MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-29-pinterest-inc-stock/) and Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/pinterest-earnings-in-focus-can-ai-tools-close-monetization-gap-93CH-4984282); TIKR has ~$1.2bn. Adj. EPS consensus $0.49 (MarketBeat $0.4863, Investing.com $0.49; Benzinga showed an older $0.41). Adj. EBITDA ~$348m and GAAP EPS ~$0.09 (TIKR, 2026-10-26). The guidance bar the stock trades on: Q4 revenue ~$1.52bn (+15% YoY), single source (TIKR https://www.tikr.com/blog/pinterest-has-fallen-after-4-of-its-last-5-earnings-reports-heres-what-october-29-needs-to-show), so the guidance findings are capped small. The revenue bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimates.
positioning_check: Short interest 46,869,291 shares = 9.10% of float, days to cover 3.8, settlement 2026-10-15, up 4.05% from 45.05m on 2026-09-30 (MarketBeat https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/PINS/short-interest/; FINRA published 2026-10-26). Elevated but not crowded. Baseline 25-delta skew is -10.65 vol points: calls are bid over puts ('upside paid'). Put/call OI 0.52. ATM spread 11.5% of mid. Straddle 12.64% (Unusual Whales shows ±10.58%). Tape: -10.84% over 5 days, +5.06% over 20 days, -39% from the 52-week high, and about -4.8% intraday on the print day (MarketBeat showed $19.92 at 14:14 ET). The 5.5% drop on 2026-10-26 was attributed to pre-earnings de-risking and the CFO handover, with no operating news (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Pinterest+shares+slide+as+investors+position+ahead+of+earnings+and+absorb+CFO+transition).

findings.finding: Pinterest has beaten the TOP of its own revenue guide by 2-3% in each of the last two quarters: Q1 2026 actual $1,008m against an updated guide of $958-978m (+3.1% over the top), and Q2 2026 $1,180m against $1,133-1,153m (+2.3%). On the Q2 call the CFO said the HIGH end of the Q3 guide ($1,210m) reflects underlying performance once a 3-point drag from FX, Prime Day and World Cup timing is taken out. A repeat of the pattern puts Q3 at roughly $1.235-1.245bn against a consensus of $1.21bn, which sits at the top of the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat the top of its guide by 2.3% and the stock fell 8.68% on a Q3 guide pointing to deceleration. Q3 2025 revenue came in at the top of the guide and the stock fell 21.76% on the Q4 guide. The stock has fallen after 4 of its last 5 prints even though revenue beat in 4 of them. Revenue beats are not paid here.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $1.21bn already sits at the top of the guide, so a beat of the top is partly expected. A further ~2% is not in the published bar. If the market fully expected a repeat beat, consensus would sit above the guide range, as it does for habitual beaters. It does not.
findings.independence: Q1 guide and actual: https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/02/18/pinterest-raises-quarterly-revenue-forecast-boosted-by-tvscientific-deal and the Q1 call summary. The CFO's 'high end consistent with underlying' remark: https://ppc.land/pinterest-europe-ad-growth-drops-to-12-after-regulators-hit-asian-sellers/ (2026-08-05). Same company-guidance family as the Q2 release.

findings.finding: Q4 comparisons ease in the company's own numbers: Q4 2025 revenue grew only 14% (US & Canada +9%, $979m, during the large-retailer pullback) against 17% in Q3 2025. tvScientific (closed 2026-02-17, $465m consideration) adds inorganic CTV revenue until February 2027. The street's Q4 bar is about $1.52bn, +15%. Holding Q2's US & Canada growth of 18% on a +9% comp is above that bar, so the comp gives a guide above $1.52bn room.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide decides the reaction on this name: May 2026's strong Q2 guide +6.86%; Aug 2026 Q3 guide showing deceleration -8.68%; Feb 2026 weak Q1 guide -16.83%; Nov 2025 weak Q4 guide -21.76% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: This is my arithmetic on public company numbers, and it is partly priced: the street's +15% Q4 bar already sits above Q3's guided 13-15%. Management has guided conservatively and cut the 2-year stack by about 4 points from Q2 to the Q3 guide. If that repeats, the guide lands at about $1.52bn and this finding is worth zero. If the market priced the comp fully, the Q4 bar would sit at 17-18%.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001506293/000150629326000102/q2-26xpressrelease.htm) shows US & Canada re-accelerating to +18%. The Sep 9 Goldman conference cited a US & Canada recovery and AI ad efficiency 'durable into Q3' (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/pins-stock-slides-7-after-ceo-won-t-refresh-guidance-flags-overseas-headwinds/cZt7gAcRJzC). Inference, not a company Q4 statement.

findings.finding: International drag continues and is company-confirmed. Europe revenue growth fell to +12% reported, +7% constant currency, in Q2 2026 (from +27% in Q1), because Asia-based cross-border sellers pulled back after the EU ended its €150 duty exemption on 2026-07-01. The CFO said the pressure 'is continuing in the third quarter'. On 2026-09-09, at Goldman's conference, the CEO compared it to the US tariff hit and said rebuilding the international sales model 'will create some near-term pain'; the stock fell about 7% that day. Europe's Q4 2025 comp is +25%, so the drag can also reach the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The tariff-driven large-retailer pullback (the US analogue the CEO cited) drove the -21.76% (Nov 2025) and -16.83% (Feb 2026) reactions on weak guides. The cross-border pressure was first flagged with the Q2 print, which fell 8.68%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock fell about 7% on the remarks and the Q3 guide includes the drag. What is not priced is how far it runs into Q4 against Europe's +25% comp. Europe is about 18% of revenue and US & Canada (75%) grew 18% in Q2, so net of the rest of the company this is small.
findings.independence: The Q2 call quote and the EU de minimis timing: https://ppc.land/pinterest-europe-ad-growth-drops-to-12-after-regulators-hit-asian-sellers/ (2026-08-05). Reuters via MarketScreener: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/pinterest-expects-slower-quarterly-revenue-growth-as-ad-competition-heats-up-ce7f50ded18ff621 (2026-08-04).

findings.finding: Ad demand from counterparties that reported after Pinterest last spoke is mixed to firm. Meta Q3 2026 (2026-10-21): revenue +26%, ad impressions +10%, average price per ad +14%, Q4 guide $73-76bn. Alphabet Q3 2026 (2026-10-28): Search +12%, but YouTube ads only +9% ($11,207m against $10,261m) and Google Network +1%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline series for peer read-through. Meta beat by about 2% and still fell about 7% (on costs), so good ad prints are not rewarded across the group this season (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/expect-pinterest-pins-q3-earnings-043834079.html).
findings.why_not_priced: PINS estimates were essentially flat over 30 days (Yahoo, 2026-10-27), so the Meta pricing strength has not moved the PINS bar. That is weak evidence, because Pinterest has run on its own pricing problem (pricing -5% YoY in Q1 2026). This is a proxy, and the Alphabet display and video lines nearest Pinterest's format were soft.
findings.independence: Alphabet Q3 2026 exhibit 99.1: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm (2026-10-28) points partly the other way, with YouTube at +9% and Network at +1%. Proxy only; Pinterest has not confirmed the read-through.

findings.finding: The stock was de-risked into the print: -10.84% over 5 sessions and about -4.8% intraday on the print day, at about 9.4x forward earnings. Short interest rose 4% to 9.1% of float (3.8 days to cover, 2026-10-15). Calls trade over puts (25-delta skew -10.65) and put/call OI is 0.52. The 2026-10-26 drop of 5.5% had no operating news behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Before the +6.86% May 2026 reaction the stock had been weak. The last 7 reactions split 3 up and 4 down, all large.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself, so this mostly says the bar is lower. The upside skew already reflects the asymmetry. It agrees with the skew and is therefore largely in the options price. What would not be priced is a squeeze from 47m shorts on an in-line guide.
findings.independence: The tape from the baseline and the Quiver note on de-risking with no operating news (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Pinterest+shares+slide+as+investors+position+ahead+of+earnings+and+absorb+CFO+transition, 2026-10-26).

findings.finding: Large capital-return capacity relative to the market cap. $1.95bn remains under the $3.5bn buyback announced 2026-03-03, about 17% of a market cap of roughly $11.5bn (565.5m shares at $20.4). Over $2bn was bought in H1 at an average $18.17, and share count fell about 15%. Q2 free cash flow was $270m. On 2026-10-15 the company replaced a $500m revolver with an undrawn $700m 5-year facility (SOFR+1.25%, accordion of the greater of $1bn and 75% of EBITDA). Financing question answered: the new money adds liquidity for buybacks and investment; it does not signal distress (FCF positive, nothing drawn, covenants met).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-03-03 announcement of the Elliott $1bn convertible and the $2bn near-term buyback came with the stock near its lows. There is no clean print reaction to a buyback alone in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Remaining authorization is public. What is not in the price is the pace: Q2 buybacks were only $79m after $1.94bn in Q1, and an accelerated programme or a stepped-up pace announced with results, at a price near the H1 average, would be new. If the market expected one, the stock would not trade at 9.4x forward.
findings.independence: Buyback figures: https://www.tikr.com/blog/pinterest-has-a-2-billion-buyback-the-october-29-report-tests-whether-cash-flow-can-fund-it (2026-10-28) and the Q2 release cash-flow statement (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001506293/000150629326000102/q2-26xpressrelease.htm). The revolver is from a separate document (the 8-K).

findings.finding: A new CFO started three days before the print. James Dibbo (ex-Amazon) took over on 2026-10-26; the outgoing CFO, Julia Brau Donnelly, stays as adviser and principal financial officer through 2026-10-30. This is his first call and it carries the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CFO change in the baseline window. The stock fell 5.5% on the handover day with no other news.
findings.why_not_priced: The handover is public and partly priced (the -5.5% on 10-26). The unpriced part is a guide set conservatively by a CFO who does not want to miss his first. This is inference with no document behind it, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The TIKR preview names the transition as a watch item (https://www.tikr.com/blog/pinterest-has-fallen-after-4-of-its-last-5-earnings-reports-heres-what-october-29-needs-to-show). Same event, no independent evidence of a conservative guide.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-30 the board amended the executive (Level 21) severance and change-in-control plan. A without-cause exit now pays a pro-rated target bonus; termination around a change in control pays the greater of target or actual bonus; and a cut of more than 10% in target bonus now counts as good reason. Elliott holds $1bn of 2031 convertibles.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a quiet 8-K item that nobody covers. Strengthened change-in-control terms often come before a strategic review, but nothing ties it to the print, so it is near zero unless the release mentions strategic options.

findings.finding: Insiders sold steadily into the quarter: 51 open-market sales and 0 purchases over 6 months, including co-founder Silbermann at about $37.9m (39 sales) and the outgoing CFO at about $1.39m. Form 144s and Form 4s continued through 2026-10-27.
findings.why_not_priced: Most of these look like routine 10b5-1 sales by a founder, so they carry little information. A cluster of open-market buys would have been the signal, and there is none.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing index for CIK 1506293 shows Form 144/4 filings through 2026-10-27 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001506293&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40).

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured. GAAP EPS has not been the line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: The decline is already guided, so it sits inside what the company told the market.

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the options market's upside skew and the 5-day de-risking (a low bar, calls bid), but it cuts against this name's own reaction history of selling revenue beats on the guide, so p_up sits only one point above 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the revenue beat-the-top pattern went from +0.8 to +0.4, because the Q2 beat of the top by 2.3% was sold 8.68%; p_up went from 52 to 51.

Rule 9 (segment net of the rest) and rule 6 (inside the guide): the Europe cross-border finding went from -1.0 to -0.6. Europe is about 18% of revenue, US & Canada (75%) grew 18%, and the Q3 part is inside the guide.
Rule 7 (positioning): the de-risked positioning finding went from +0.8 to +0.5, because it agrees with the upside skew and is largely in the option price.
Rule 5 (proxy): the peer finding (Meta strong, Alphabet YouTube/Network soft) went from +0.5 to +0.4 and is labelled as a proxy.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): SBC went from +0.1 to 0.0, because the decline is already guided.

Rule 4 (financing is a question): answered for the revolver. It is undrawn, FCF is positive and it adds buyback/investment liquidity, so it stays non-negative inside the capital-return finding (+0.5 unchanged).
Rule 6 (single-source bar): the Q4 bar of ~$1.52bn has one source, so the guidance findings stay capped small. CFO -0.5 to -0.4; Q4 comp finding +1.0 to +0.8.
print_vs_bar_pct went from +2.0 to +1.5 because of the continuing Europe drag inside Q3.
